This is an Infrastructure and SW task:

- leave depencency locally bound to acts-mac-studio to the spack acts ci-depenencies
- make sure that in nodd we have a folder/directory for the software with (whereever possible gitmodules)
  - then `software/submodules`
    - make ACTS a git submodule of this folder
    - make IdRes a submodule  
    - make nodehammer a submodule 
    - make ... whatever you had prepared already a submodule 
  - then actual `software/source` for source code
    - our event processing framework for this should still be ActsExamples, however additional Algorithms go into the `sofware/source/ActsExamples` locally and not into the checked out Acts repo (currently acts-nodd) 
    - necessary glue code to work with externals should go here
    - DD4hep code for building the detector should go here, `software/source/detectors`, the ACTS related part can go into `sofware/source/ActsExamples` the DD4hep part should be self-contained
    - Additional EDM should go here etc. 
  - then steering and running `software/running`
    - python based steering files for doing jobs
  - then analysis `software/analysis`



Create the Makefiles for this and a number of PRs that set this up step by step to arrive at the same functionality you have right now (including `acts-nodd`).



The objective is:

- updating Acts would be a single git submodule operation (and would not touch code specific to nodd), if updates to nodd-code are needed after an ACTS code update this can be tested
- detector code is independent and can be encapsulated 



Ask if something is not clear.

I’ll inspect the current repositories and build setup, then organize the migration into reviewable PRs while preserving the existing functionality and the Spack dependency binding on `acts-mac-studio`.

I’m using the [acts-spack skill]([redacted] to verify the existing dependency environment. I also found several nODD worktrees, so I’ll use an isolated checkout for this migration and preserve their current work.

The Spack preflight recognizes `acts-mac-studio-01.cern.ch`, but its recorded setup and lockfile fingerprints have changed. I’ll verify the active runtime before building. The `acts-nodd` checkout also contains uncommitted nODD changes; I’ll preserve them and include the relevant functionality in the migration.
Which repository URL should I use for the IdRes submodule? The existing intake record pins commit d54d0e3c465cc0308becb737b04364ce5c68ce16, but does not record a publishable clone URL.

The runtime checks passed with the current Spack environment: DD4hep 1.38, Geant4 11.4.2, and all 12 datasets. I’m planning three stacked PRs: pinned dependencies and Makefiles, detector source encapsulation, then local ActsExamples extensions with steering and analysis. The ACTS submodule will contain no nODD-specific code.

I found prepared calorimeter reconstruction, jet finding, and EDM4hep persistence code in the separate ACTS branch. I’ll include it in a fourth PR. I’m also retaining the existing ODD comparison source as a pinned submodule, with its large data assets handled separately.

The detector migration preserves the baseline: all 16 tracker XML files are byte-for-byte identical, and the 680,292-entry entity inventory is unchanged. The DD4hep component now configures independently of ACTS. I’m testing the local extensions against a clean ACTS checkout without modifying its source files.

The full detector regression suite passed all 10 checks. The clean ACTS build exposed two Python generator packages that the old workflow supplied implicitly. I’ll make that setup explicit in a build-owned Python environment while keeping compiled dependencies in the existing Spack installation.

The first two PRs are open. The new build keeps the ACTS submodule clean and compiles nODD targets from `software/source/ActsExamples`. The existing Python sensitivity controls are now provided locally as well. The remaining checks cover Gen3 navigation, Geant4 material recording, and calorimeter persistence.

I’ll use that IdRes fork and keep the recorded revision where it is available. The migrated tracker job has passed: 45,646 sensor surfaces, 117 volumes, and 128 straight navigation tracks. I’ll add IdRes to the first PR and finish the calorimeter migration.

IdRes is pinned at the original revision from the fork you supplied. It built with Spack GSL, and all 22 adapter runs passed. The migrated ActsExamples tests passed all 10 checks, including Geant4 material recording; the calorimeter, jet, and EDM4hep suite also passed all 10 checks. I’m finishing the PR stack and its validation records.

CI caught a bookkeeping issue in the detector move: the initial placeholder README prevented Git from recognizing the existing README as a rename. I’ll correct that without changing the CI policy. The optional nodehammer native build is also running against the current Spack environment.

All four PRs are open, and the corrected stack passes the unchanged project-record policy locally. Nodehammer finished its native build with all 602 tests passing. I’m closing the session records and checking the final remote heads.

The remaining CI failure is in the moved detector README: I counted one directory level too many in its relative links. I’ll correct the links and run the documentation checks locally before pushing the fix.

Created four stacked PRs. Merge in this order:

1. [#77 — Submodules and Makefiles](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/77)
2. [#78 — Independent DD4hep detector sources](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/78)
3. [#79 — Local ActsExamples, steering and analysis](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/79)
4. [#80 — Calorimeter, EDM and external adapters](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/80)

ACTS remains a clean submodule, with nODD code outside it. The existing Spack binding is preserved.

Passed: 10 detector, 10 adapter, 10 calorimeter tests; 22 IdRes runs; 602 nodehammer tests; and native/Gen3 geometry comparison. Latest #80 CI is still running.
